 Judgment

The mother and sister of deceased one Nazeemudheen, S/o. Abdul Rab, have filed this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal against the Judgment and Decree dated 17.02.2021 made in M.C.O.P.No.528 of 2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Special District Court, Salem, for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Special District Court, Salem
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2.The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, read with Rule 3 of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Rules for claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the death of one Nazeemudheen, who died in the road accident that has occurred on 30.12.2017.

3.According to claimants, on 30.12.2017 at 11.00 P.M., while the deceased Nazeemudheen and one Prabakaran were returning from Ayyothiyapattinam to Salem Town in bullet motorcycle bearing Registration No.TN 54 M 3773. at Masinaickenpatti Bridge near Ravi Auto Carriage, an Eicher Van bearing Registration No.TN 04 L 6096 came in a rash and negligent manner, hit against the bullet motorcycle driven by the deceased Nazeemudheen and due to the said impact, the said Nazeemudheen and his https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis friend Prabakaran were thrown out from the bullet motorcycle and the said Nazeemudheen died on the spot itself, is not in dispute.
4.The Tribunal after hearing both side arguments and upon considering the oral and documentary evidence has awarded compensation for a sum of Rs.11,86,680/-.
5.The learned counsel for the appellants would strenuously argue that monthly income fixed by the Tribunal in respect of the deceased, who was pursuing his first year BCA course at Rs.9,000/- is less.
No amount was awarded for loss of love and affection and for transportation.
For not wearing protective head gear, the Tribunal fixed 15% contributory negligence is incorrect and prayed for enhancement of compensation.

To strengthen his above said arguments, the learned counsel for appellants relied the following judgment:
(i) Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (VPM) Ltd., Vs.
R.Natarajan, reported in [2023 (1) TNMAC 191 (DB)].
6.

entities.text:
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (VPM) Ltd., Vs.
R.Natarajan, reported in [2023 (1) TNMAC 191 (DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Per contra, the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent  Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
would argue that considering the age and year of accident, the monthly income of the deceased may be fixed as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rs.12,000/-.

7.Heard the arguments of learned counsel for appellants, 1st respondent as well as respondents 2 &
4 and perused the materials on record.
8.

From perusal of the available materials, it is seen that the Tribunal has fixed 15% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased Nazeemudheen for not wearing protective head gear at the time of accident.
The said ground was not pleaded by the 2nd respondent in the counter before the Tribunal.
Hence, 15% contributory negligence fixed on the part of deceased is set aside.

Shameem vs N.Gopi on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147245973/
2 9.Regarding the income of the deceased, the Tribunal has fixed notional income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- per month, for a first year BCA student, which according to learned counsel for appellants is so meagre.

entities.text:
Shameem vs N.Gopi on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147245973/
2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10.Further

, this Court in Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (VPM) Ltd.,
Vs. R.Natarajan, reported in [2023 (1) TNMAC 191 (DB)], wherein it has been observed that the Tribunal has https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis taken Rs.15,000/- as notional monthly income.

entities.text: Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (VPM) Ltd.
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text:
In 2018, the salary drawn by a last grade Government servant was around Rs.20,000/- therefore,
adoption of Rs.15,000/- as notional income for a student cannot be said to be on the higher side.
11. Based on the afore mentioned observations, in order to have effective justice, this Court deems fit to fix the income of the deceased at Rs.14,000/- per month.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in 2017 (2) TN MAC 609 (SC),
has standardised the details of future prospects, for the age group of persons below 40 years as 40%.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in 2017 (2) TN MAC 609 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. The date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 20.08.1998 as per Ex.P1  Driving Licence,
Ex.P12 Mark Sheet and Ex.P13-Transfer Certificate.
Therefore, at the relevant point of time, age of the deceased was 19 years.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma &
others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & another reported in 2009 (2) TNMAC 1 SC, for the age group of persons between 15 to 25 years, the multiplier to be adopted is 18.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma &
others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & another reported in 2009 (2) TNMAC 1 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus the loss of dependency is re- worked as follows:
Age of the deceased : 19 years https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

Income of the deceased fixed:
Rs.14,000/-
After adding 40% Future Prospects : Rs.14,000/- + 40% = Rs.5,600/-
Rs.14,000/-+Rs.5,600/-
= Rs.19,600/-
Deduction towards personal and living expenses : 50%. Rs.19,600/- / 2 = Rs.9,800/-
Loss of Dependency : Rs.9,800/- X 12 X 18 Rs.21,16,800/-.
Towards loss of consortium, the appellants are entitled to Rs.20,000/- each.
An amount of Rs.5,000/- is granted towards transport expenses.
In all other aspects, the amount awarded by the Tribunal shall stands confirmed.

13.Thus, the amounts awarded by the Tribunal is modified as follows:

3
1 . For Loss of 11,56,680/- 21,16,800/- E  dependency  2. For Loss of 15,000/- 15,000/- C  Estate  3.

For Loss of filial -  consortium to 1st 20,000/- 
 appellant  4. For Loss of love -  and affection to 20,000/- 
 2nd appellant  5. For - 5,000/- 
 Transportation  Charges https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
6. For Funeral 15,000/- 15,000/- C  expenses

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.11,86,680/- to Rs.21,91,800/- which would carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

15. In the result,
(i) The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed.
No costs.
(ii) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.11,86,680/- to Rs.21,91,800/-.

(iii) The 2nd respondent-Reliance General Insurance Company Limited is directed to deposit the award amount, now determined by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment,
to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.528 of 2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Special District Court, Salem.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(iv) On such deposit, the 1st appellant, who is the mother of the deceased is permitted to withdraw a sum of Rs.16,43,850/- as her share of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the award amount and the Shameem vs N.Gopi on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147245973/
4

2nd appellant, who is the sister of the deceased is permitted to withdraw a sum of Rs.5,47,950/-, as her share of the award amount along with proportionate interest and costs, less the amount if any,
already withdrawn by making necessary cheque applications before the Tribunal.
The appellants are directed to pay the necessary Court fee for the enhanced award amount now determined by this Court.
This appeal is dismissed as against the respondents 3 and 4.
